_comment: A5 Hand-computed golden fixture expected results. All values computed from first principles — do not update without recomputing by hand.

fixture_perfect.description: 100 trades, 70 winners @ $100 gross, 30 losers @ -$66.67 gross, MES $0.62/side commission

derivation.sharpe_note: All 100 net P&Ls used. winners=98.76 (70 of them), losers=-67.91 (30 of them). mean = (70×98.76 + 30×(-67.91))/100 = (6913.20 - 2037.30)/100 = 48.759. std(ddof=1) computed over 100 values where 70 are 98.76 and 30 are -67.91. Sharpe = mean/std * sqrt(252).
derivation.max_dd_note: Trades listed winners first then losers. Equity curve: first 70 trades accumulate $98.76 each, peaking at $6913.20, then 30 losers take it to $4875.90. Max DD from peak = $6913.20 - $4875.90 = $2037.30.

expected.notes: Fixture 1 focuses on: (a) gross PF correctly computed from gross P&Ls, (b) net PF correctly computed from net P&Ls after commission, (c) total commission = n_trades × commission_per_trade, (d) net_pnl = sum of net_pnl column.

fixture_losing.description: 200 trades, 40 winners (20%) @ $150 gross, 160 losers @ -$100 gross. PF = 0.375. MC ruin > 95%.

derivation.pattern: Winner at every 5th trade position (4,9,14,...,199) = 40 winners, 160 losers
derivation.mc_ruin_argument: Pattern: every 5 trades = 4 losers (-$404.96) + 1 winner ($148.76) = net -$256.20 per 5 trades = -$51.24/trade. Starting from $50,000, ruin at $47,500 (5% drawdown = $2,500). Avg loss $51.24/trade → expected ruin in ~49 trades. Any 4-loss sequence = -$404.96 drawdown. P(ruin) >> 95% over 200-trade path.

expected.notes: Fixture 2 (path-based MC test) focuses on: (a) gross PF 0.375 correctly computed, (b) MC ruin probability > 95% when ruin_threshold=$47,500 and n_sims=10,000. Actual win rate is 20% (every 5th trade wins). The gross PF 0.375 << 1.0 guarantees catastrophic ruin.

fixture_marginal.description: 100 trades, 60 winners @ $87 gross, 40 losers @ -$75 gross. PF 1.74, below 1.75 promotion gate.

derivation.gate_outcome: gross_pf=1.74 < 1.75 → DOES NOT PROMOTE. net_pf=1.687 also < 1.75.

expected.notes: Fixture 3 (promotion gate test) focuses on: (a) gross PF = exactly 1.740 (just below gate), (b) net PF = 1.687 (also below gate), (c) test asserts net_pf < 1.75, which means the strategy DOES NOT cross the promotion threshold. This catches bugs where the gate uses gross instead of net PF, or rounds incorrectly.

fixture_regime_shift.description: 200 trades in 2 epochs: early (trades 1-100, PF=7.2), late (trades 101-200, PF=0.444). Walk-forward shows dramatic degradation.

early_epoch.net_pnl_note: net_pnl column = gross_pnl (no commission subtracted in fixture). Sum = $9,000 - $1,250 = $7,750.

late_epoch.net_pnl_note: net_pnl column = gross_pnl (no commission subtracted). Sum = $2,000 - $4,500 = -$2,500.

derivation.walk_forward_expectation: Fold 1 (early, PF=7.2) vs Fold 2 (late, PF=0.44). Degradation ratio 16x >> minimum 4x. Classic regime collapse pattern.
derivation.net_pnl_column_note: The fixture stores net_pnl = gross_pnl for simplicity. Tests should use gross_pf computed from gross_pnl for PF checks, and net_pnl column sum for PnL checks.

expected.notes: Fixture 4 (walk-forward degradation). Early PF=7.2, Late PF=0.44, degradation ratio=16x >> 4x minimum. net_pnl column = gross_pnl in this fixture (no commission deduction). Tests use gross_pf for PF assertions and sum(net_pnl) for PnL assertions.

fixture_fees_killer.description: 200 trades, 100 winners @ $10 gross, 100 losers @ -$6.25 gross. Tradeify commission $1.29/side. Gross PF=1.60, net PF=0.840.

derivation.key_insight: Gross PF=1.6 looks profitable. Net PF=0.84 is a loser. The commission on each losing trade ADDS to the loss (net loss = gross loss + commission), making the denominator of PF larger. The commission on each winning trade SUBTRACTS from the gain, making the numerator smaller. Both effects compound.
derivation.vectorbt_bug_test: If test asserts net_pf < 1.0 but system returns net_pf > 1.0, it means fees are NOT being applied to losses — they are only being subtracted from wins. This is the classic vectorbt futures P&L bug where slippage/fees are passed as % of trade value, not applied per-contract.

expected.net_pf_check: net_pf < 1.0 (strategy is a loser after fees)
expected.notes: Fixture 5 (fees killer) is the critical bug-detection fixture. If the system computes net_pf > 1.0, fees are not being correctly applied — specifically, they are not being added to losing trades. The test must assert BOTH that gross_pf > 1.5 AND net_pf < 1.0 to confirm the transition. This is the exact class of bug that kills live prop traders who run gross-only backtests.
